title: Measure a new brake rotor's thickness with an outside micrometer
instruction: Measure the brake rotor's thickness at the marked spot with the outside micrometer, and leave the micrometer on the reading, back on its rest.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, about 0.7 million employed in the US, BLS OEWS approximate) measure brake rotor thickness at every brake job against the discard thickness stamped on the rotor; incoming new rotors are checked the same way before fitting. The standard tool is a 0-25 mm outside micrometer: one hand holds the frame square on the rotor's friction band and rocks it slightly across the face (the manufacturers' technique for finding the true, smallest reading), the other turns the ratchet knob until it clicks (it slips at the 5-10 N measuring force), then the micrometer is lifted off with the reading showing on the thimble.
setup: Left and right are the robot's; positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the table. A new 280 x 22.0 mm internally vented front brake rotor (Brembo 09.7012.11, for the 2001-05 VW Golf IV 1.8T GTI and Audi A3 8L: 280 mm dia, 22.0 mm new, 37 mm overall height, 65 mm centre bore, 5 x 100 mm stud holes, 5.86 kg grey cast iron) is fixed on a 6061-T6 aluminium hub stand (200 x 200 x 12 mm base, 70 x 16 x 140 mm column, 90 mm dia x 12 mm flange), its axis along y at z 0.152 m, centre x 0.508, y 0.120; nearest rim x 0.368. A 2 mm paint dot marks the scored spot on the outboard face at 135 mm from the hub axis, 10 degrees above the 9 o'clock line (facing the robot). A 0-25 mm outside micrometer of the Mitutoyo 103-137 class (free: 175 g, 18 mm thimble, 6.35 mm faces, 0.5 mm pitch, ratchet stop, lock lever, spindle fully open at 25.0 mm) lies across the two 46 x 6 x 146 mm uprights of a 6061-T6 rest (80 x 80 x 30 mm base, 36 mm clear gap, 0.8 mm EPDM caps) at x 0.330, y 0.165, its axis along y, its throat toward +x. A real trial measures the reference thickness at the dot (README).
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged as things stand at the end. (1) The micrometer was closed square on the rotor's friction band at the marked spot: its anvil face centre 100 to 136 mm from the hub axis and within 5 mm of the dot, the anvil on the rotor's face (within 1 mm), its axis within 5 degrees of the hub axis, and the reading within +-0.02 mm of the rotor's measured thickness at the dot (22.00 mm in the sim; the new rotor's actual value measured per real trial, README; +-0.05 mm only with a 0.01 mm-grade reference). (2) With step 1, the ratchet clicked (slipped a tooth) at least twice with the faces on the rotor. (3) With step 2, the micrometer is off the rotor and its reading is within +-0.02 mm of that measured thickness. (4) With step 3, the micrometer lies on its rest (within 12 mm, 4 mm up, 6 degrees), no gripper holds it and no pad is within 3 cm. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four have held together for 1 s with the micrometer within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8. Scoring 0 for the whole run: the micrometer falling off the table, or dropped (falling faster than 0.6 m/s with nothing holding it).
reset_notes: Lay the micrometer across the rest's ribs with the spindle fully open (25.0 mm), the lock lever unlocked and the ratchet at rest. Nothing is held; the rotor, dot and rest stay fixed.
fidelity: Declared: the thread (0.5 mm a turn), the ratchet (0.006 N m slip, 18-degree clicks: estimates), the measuring force (6 N from a 0.03 mm lag; drive capped at 10 N). After the faces close the drive follows the spindle closing, never opening, so rocking settles the minimum. The +-0.02 mm band applies (sim and real with a 0.001 mm reference; +-0.05 mm with 0.01 mm); the sim's reference is 22.00 mm, a real trial's is measured at the dot (median of five). Frame sizes and lever are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (hit the step limit); demo: 1.0 on MuJoCo at step 2792 (kept reading 22.015 mm); Isaac demo rerun pending for the new rotor
